docs.text:
User manual for SegDisp v1.0.x · Compatible with Blender 5.1 (minimum 5.1.1).

Patch-specific instructions: A tag icon followed by a version label identifies instructions that apply only to the stated patch version or version range (for example, v1.0.1 only or v1.0.1 and later).

Blender Compatibility

SegDisp v1.0.1 has been tested with Blender 5.1.2, the recommended version for this release. The declared minimum requirement remains Blender 5.1.1, but v1.0.1 has not yet been re-tested on that version.

Note for Lite edition users:

The Segment Display Lite edition does not have a separate user manual. However, Lite users can still reference this manual for the Installation, Activation, Troubleshooting, and Settings & Preferences sections, as they apply to both editions. Exception: Lite's asset recovery procedure differs from Pro's and is not covered in this manual. The remaining sections (such as Input Categories) cover Pro-specific features, but may still be useful as a general reference.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Segment Display Pro is a Blender add-on that lets you create, customize, and animate segment displays entirely inside Blender using procedural Geometry Nodes. It supports multiple display types, including 7-segment and 16-segment layouts, giving you the flexibility to recreate a wide range of real-world electronic readouts.

Whether you're building digital clocks, calculators, speedometers, control panels, scoreboards, or price tags, the add-on handles the full pipeline: from generating the display geometry to controlling individual characters, styles, colors, and animations, all from a dedicated N-panel interface without any manual modeling.

docs.title: v1.0.1
docs.text:
Released: 2026/11/08  ·  Requires: Blender 5.1 (Minimum 5.1.1)  ·  Tested and recommended: Blender 5.1.2

A patch release with an About section and manual update checks, a Pro-only Review & Recover workflow for asset problems, and clearer asset and version notices. This patch has not yet been re-tested on Blender 5.1.1.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• About: in Preferences and at the bottom of the N-panel, showing Add-on Version, Assets Version, Compatible Blender and developer credits. See About Panel.
  • Check for Updates: a manual check in About, alongside the existing startup check. Open Downloads opens the release page; installation stays manual. See Add-on Update.
  • Hide update notifications: an option to hide the N-panel header update notice. Update information remains available in About and Preferences. The preference is saved in addon_userpref.json outside the add-on folder, so it survives normal updates; for now it stores only this preference.
  • Review & Recover (Pro): in Preferences > Asset Status. Preview supported library reconnections and missing node-tree repairs, review uncertain cases and pick the right modifier, optionally recreate a missing modifier with default settings, back up an already saved project first, and repair toggle inputs stored as numbers while keeping their on/off values. See Review & Recover.
  • Recognition properties: segdisp_* custom properties on Pro objects help recovery recognize displays. See Pro recognition properties.
  • Email Support: a new button in Resources & Support that opens your default mail app. See Resources & Support.

docs.title: Improved
docs.text:
• Review & Recover replaces the visible Re-link Asset button in Pro. Library reconnections can affect displays across scenes, and results show which items were left unchanged and which settings could not be restored.
  • Add Segment Display checks for a missing asset or a known asset/add-on version mismatch before adding a display.
  • Clearer asset availability, version mismatch and restart-required notices. Unavailable asset versions show as Unknown instead of a misleading value.
  • N-panel asset warnings include a shortcut to Preferences.
  • About and Viewport & Overlays start collapsed in the N-panel.
  • Resources & Support documentation links point to the versioned v1.0 manual.

docs.title: Update Notes
docs.text:
Before and after updating

  • Install the new complete Pro ZIP over the existing add-on, then restart Blender before troubleshooting. Keep a project backup before running any repair. See Updating the Add-on.
  • Recovery does not save over your open project or guarantee that deleted settings come back. Review the result, then save.
  • Blender may stop responding for a while during asset processing. Let it finish.
  • Local asset copies, objects from the other edition and source-linked modifiers are not repaired directly. Linking displays from another project is not a validated workflow.
  • Do not modify the segdisp_type, segdisp_schema, segdisp_edition or segdisp_modifier custom properties.
  • License seat limits and the 14-day offline policy are unchanged.

docs.title: v1.0.0 (Initial Release)
docs.text:
Released: 2026/10/18  ·  Requires: Blender 5.1 (Minimum 5.1.1)

The first public release of Segment Display Pro.

docs.title: Input Categories
docs.text:
• Numbers: numeric readouts in Simple mode (up to 8 digits) or Complex mode (up to 15 digits across five input groups), with decimals and minus sign. Complex mode keeps long numbers accurate, with no rounding errors. See the Troubleshooting page.
  • Alphanumeric: text and character readouts on up to 3 displays, with alignment options.
  • Time: Clock, Timer and Date readouts. Can animate automatically in sync with the scene time (12/24-hour format, time direction, start offset).

docs.title: Display
docs.text:
• 7-segment and 16-segment display models.
  • Segment Thickness, Segment Gap and Display Angle (straight to italic).
  • 7-segment alternative fonts for the digits 6, 7 and 9.
  • 16-segment Font Width (full/narrow), Font Align and Font Alternatives.
  • Horizontal and vertical align, Display Size, digit and character spacing, Minus Sign Offset, Decimal Size and Decimal Vertical Position.
  • Light-Emitting (LED) and Monochrome (LCD-style) display materials.

docs.title: Separators
docs.text:
• Whole and decimal separators (colons, dots, dashes and more), each configurable on its own.
  • Digit-style separator character: uses a segment digit as a separator, with its own segment model, segment count and Segment Gap.
  • Separators in between characters and displays.

docs.title: Viewport & Overlays
docs.text:
• Solid Viewport Preview: see LED segments in Solid shading.
  • Ghost Segments: shows the inactive (unlit) segments in the viewport for easier layout. Useful if the LED Base is hidden or not toggled.
  • Z-Offset: sets the gap between the LED segments and the display base. Also fixes flickering when the display is viewed from far away.

docs.title: Add-on
docs.text:
• "SegDisp Pro" tab in the 3D Viewport sidebar (N-panel).
  • "Add Segment Display" button, adds the object at the 3D cursor.
  • Fully procedural Geometry Nodes setup. All display objects share one linked asset file.
  • Works with EEVEE and Cycles.
  • License key activation and deactivation (Lemon Squeezy), 3 activation seats. Activation survives restarts, updates, reinstalls and new Blender versions (requires an online check at least every 14 days).
  • Offline license notices: a red warning at the top of the N-panel and in Preferences during the last 3 days of the 14-day offline period, and when the add-on is locked. "Read more..." explains the steps and "Verify now" checks the license online right away.
  • "Asset Status" section in Preferences with a "Re-link Asset" button.

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
Known Limitations

  • Auto time animations only work with whole-number frame rates (24, 25, 30, 60, ...).
  • Only one Display Style is available for now. More styles are planned.
  • Harmless "VFont -> Node" warnings may appear in the System Console after reloading scripts or relinking assets.
  • Only tested on Windows 11 and Blender's default add-on folder.

docs.title: Display Options
docs.text: The display is the core visual element of any segment display, the panel of illuminated segments that forms each digit or character. In real-world electronics, displays vary in segment count (7-segment for simple digits, 14 or 16-segment for full alphanumeric characters), thickness, angle, and overall styling. SegDisp Pro gives you full control over the display model, segment appearance, font variations, alignment, spacing, sizing, and material properties. This section covers all display-related inputs across four panels: Models & Styles, Segment Fonts, Align/Spacing/Size, and Appearances.

docs.title: Display | Models & Styles
docs.text:
[1] Segment Display Models: Selects the segment display model used for your digits and letters (e.g., 7-segment, 16-segment).

[2] Display Styles: Selects a visual style preset for the segment display.

Info

Only a single style is currently available. Additional styles are under development and will be included in future versions.

[3] Segment Thickness: Controls the thickness of individual segments in the display.

[4] Segment Gap: Adjusts the gap between individual segments within each character.

[5] Display Angle: Sets the display angle between straight and sheared (italicized) orientations.

docs.title: 7-Segment Fonts
docs.text:
Font - A Font - B

Switches to an alternative font variation. This option is limited to the digits 6, 9, and 7.

docs.title: 16-Segment Fonts
docs.text:
The 16-segment display unlocks a wide range of font possibilities, thanks to its higher segment count.

[1] Font Width: Sets the font to "Wide" (full width of the display base) or "Narrow" (half width). Note: Not available with the 7-Segment Display Model due to segment count limitations.

[2] Font Align: Aligns the font to the left or right side of the display base when "Narrow" is selected as the font width.

[3] Font Alternatives: Selects alternative font variations for numeric and alphabetic characters.

  • Number Fonts: Sets the font variation per digit. The digit list changes with Font Width and Font Align, because each layout has a different number of segments to work with. Some digits also have more variations than others.
    • Wide: All digits, 0 to 9.
    • Narrow + Left: 2, 5, 6, 7, and 9.
    • Narrow + Right: 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 9.
  • Alphanum Fonts: Sets the font variation (A, B, or C) for letters. The 3A, 3B, and 3C rows in the image show each variation.

Info

The UI in the image above is cropped to fit the layout. Your panel may show more rows, depending on the selected Font Width and Font Align.

docs.title: Display | Align, Spacing, and Size
docs.text:
[1] Display Horizontal & Vertical Align: Aligns the display origin along both the horizontal and vertical axes.

[2] Display Size: Controls the overall scale of the display.

Tip

Alignment and sizing options can be used to stack multiple display objects together.

[3] Digit Spaces: Controls the distance between digits of whole and decimal numbers in the Numbers and Time categories.

To enable spacing options, you need a display and a decimal length of at least two.

[3] Character Space: Controls the distance between character spaces in the Alphanumeric category.

This option appears only if the Alphanumeric category is selected.

[4] Minus Sign Offset: Adjusts the minus sign offset relative to the display in the Numbers category.

[5] Decimal Size: Scales the decimal portion as a percentage relative to the main display size.

[6] Decimal Vertical Position: Sets the vertical position of the decimal portion relative to the display. Vertical Manual Position: Provides a custom manual vertical position value for the decimal portion.

docs.title: Display | Appearances
docs.text:
[1] Display Material: Selects the material applied to the display.

  • Light-Emitting: A glowing LED material where active segments emit light and inactive segments appear as a dark monochrome tone, creating the classic on-off contrast of real LED displays. Found on elevator floor indicators, electronic scoreboards, industrial control panels, gas station price signs, and digital alarm clocks.
  • Monochrome: A flat, non-emitting material where segments appear as solid dark shapes against a neutral background, with no glow or lighting effect. Mimics passive LCD panels found on calculators, digital watches, and air conditioning controllers, where segments are always visible but never illuminate.

docs.title: LED
docs.text:
[2] Toggle Led: Enables or disables the LED emission effect on the display segments.

Info

This option is currently located in the Appearances panel, which has no direct relationship to it. A new feature called "Actions" is planned for the Segment Display Pro edition. All animation-related toggles will be moved to the new panel when it is implemented in the future.

[3] Emission Color & Strength: Sets the color and intensity of the LED emission on active (lit) segments.

Info

The strength option is not available for passive LED materials.

docs.title: LED Base
docs.text:
[4] Toggle Led Base: Enables or disables the display base panel behind the segments.

[5] Base | Top/Side Colors: Sets the color of the side/top surfaces of the base behind active segments. Each LED material has its own specific color settings.

[6] Minus Sign Base Visibility: Keeps the minus sign base permanently visible, even when the minus sign is disabled in the Numbers panel.

[7] Minus Sign Base Style: Selects whether to display the complete digit base or only the the minus sign's base.

[8] Digit Separator Base Style: Selects whether to display the complete digit base or only the separator segment variations. For a more realistic look, select "Whole Display."

[9] Base Z Offset & Thickness: Controls the distance from the display base to the LED surface and the overall thickness of the base panel.

docs.title: Asset Recovery
docs.text:
v1.0.1 and later

What you can do LITE PRO Recovery tool Simple Re-link Asset button Review & Recover panel that previews every fix Reconnect the asset file Re-links the whole project in one go You pick which library to reconnect, across all scenes Reconnect a display's missing node setup Basic: only displays it can recognize Restore Node Tree; asks you to confirm when it isn't sure which modifier to fix Rebuild a deleted SegDisp modifier No Optional, only for SegDisp objects, rebuilt with default settings Back up your project before recovery No (Lite has no recovery dialog) Yes; if the backup fails, recovery stops and nothing changes Fix on/off switches that turned into number fields No Yes, and it keeps your on/off choices Fix displays linked from another .blend file No No (fix them in the original file)

Recovery only reconnects what's still in your file. It can't bring back deleted settings or animation.

Tip: Reinstalling the matching add-on version and restarting Blender often fixes displays without any recovery.

Lite's recovery steps aren't covered in this manual. See Pro Review & Recover.

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text: Quick answers to the most common questions about Segment Display Pro and Segment Display Lite.

docs.title: The Lite Edition
docs.text:
Is there a free version of the Segment Display add-on?

Yes. There is a free version of the add-on called "Segment Display Lite". The Lite version is not a demo product. It's just a simplified variant with some limited features compared to the Pro version, for anyone who wants to discover the add-on. You can review the Edition Features Table to compare both versions.

Does Segment Display Lite have a time trial period?

No, the free version has no time trial. You can use it until a large asteroid hits the Earth!

Will the Lite version receive updates in the future?

No. For major future updates and releases, we focus all our efforts on the Pro version. The Lite version will only receive occasional hotfix patches.

Are the Lite and Pro versions independent add-ons?

Yes, they are completely different add-ons; both editions have their own assets and plugins. You do not have to install the Pro version on top of the Lite version. Both can be used on the same system. Keep in mind that you cannot control a Lite object through the Pro N-panel interface, and vice versa.

docs.title: Installation & Updates
docs.text:
Which Blender versions are supported?

v1.0.1 and later

SegDisp v1.0.1 has been tested with Blender 5.1.2, the recommended version for this release. The declared minimum is Blender 5.1.1, but v1.0.1 has not yet been re-tested on that version. Newer Blender versions are not confirmed as supported yet. The add-on runs on Windows, macOS and Linux (tested on Windows 11 only), and works with both the Cycles and EEVEE render engines. If a future add-on update needs a newer Blender version, the add-on will notify you. See the Installation & Activation page for the full system requirements.

How do I update the add-on without losing my activation?

Install the complete matching ZIP over the old version with Target Path set to Default and Overwrite enabled, then restart Blender. Your activation file is outside the add-on folder. Reopen and inspect your project first: displays often return automatically. For Pro v1.0.1 and later, use Review & Recover… only if supported issues remain after the installed asset is available. See Updating the Add-on.

Does Check for Updates install the update?

v1.0.1 and later

No. Check for Updates only checks whether a newer version is available. If there is one, Open Downloads opens the download page in your browser. Nothing is downloaded, installed or restarted for you. Download the new ZIP, install it over your current version, then restart Blender. See Add-on Update and Updating the Add-on.

How do I repair displays after an update or reinstall?

Pro v1.0.1 and later

If displays appear as planes, preserve a project copy and leave their modifiers untouched. Reinstall the complete matching add-on and restart Blender first; this often restores displays without manual recovery. If problems remain, use Preferences > Add-ons > Segment Display Pro > Asset Status > Review & Recover…. Review the actions and backup option, recover, inspect settings/animation and save.

Reconnection uses data still present. Deleted settings and animation cannot be restored by assigning a node tree again or recreating a modifier with defaults. Lite uses a different recovery procedure, not covered here. See Review & Recover.

Why is Add unavailable after updating?

Restart Blender first, then check Asset Status. Not Available means the installed asset cannot be used; Unknown version information needs checking, and a known asset/add-on version mismatch can block adding displays. Reinstall the complete matching package rather than mixing asset/script versions or editing modifiers. See asset troubleshooting.

Why did Blender stop responding during recovery?

Blender can pause while recovery relocates and reloads an asset library whose path points outside the current installation. Allow it to finish; duration varies and a temporary not-responding message does not necessarily mean a crash. This involves Blender's library handling; the exact bottleneck is unconfirmed. See recovery pauses.

docs.title: Licensing & Usage
docs.text:
Does the add-on require a license key to be activated?

Yes. Both the Lite and Pro versions require license activation through your Lemon Squeezy account. After purchasing, you'll need to activate your license key to use the add-on. You can manage your license and activations directly from your Lemon Squeezy account dashboard.

How many devices can I activate my license on?

Each Segment Display Pro license key includes 3 activations (Segment Display Lite includes 1). Every time you activate the add-on on a new device, it counts toward your limit. If you need to move your license to a different machine, make sure to deactivate it on the old device first.

Important

Uninstalling the add-on without deactivating does not free up the activation slot. If you accidentally uninstall without deactivating, you can free up the slot yourself from your Lemon Squeezy order dashboard.

Does the add-on work on render farms?

Render-farm workflows have not been tested with SegDisp, so compatibility, setup requirements and activation requirements for render nodes are not confirmed. We cannot currently guarantee that projects using live procedural SegDisp objects will render correctly on a cloud or network render farm.

You can apply the display's Geometry Nodes modifier and use the resulting mesh outside Blender, as explained under Sharing & Exporting. This is allowed, but it is not a tested render-farm workflow.

Can I use the add-on in commercial projects?

Yes. Segment Display Pro uses a dual license:

  • Add-on code (GPL v3): You're free to use, copy, and modify the code for your own pipeline. If you distribute a modified version, you must pass on the same freedoms and source code.
  • Assets (Single User Commercial License): The supplied asset .blend file remains the property of Orion November Studio and must not be redistributed, sold, shared, sub-licensed, or uploaded, in original or modified form. This restriction does not prevent you from using your generated SegDisp objects in commercial projects, including applying their modifiers and exporting the resulting meshes for use in game engines or other software.

In short: you can use your renders and generated display meshes in your projects; you cannot redistribute the supplied asset .blend file. Full details are in our license terms.

docs.title: Add-on In Action
docs.text:
Why does the add-on link assets instead of appending them to the scene?

The Segment Display Geometry Nodes asset references numerous external objects and collections required for correct functionality. Appending the asset would automatically import all of those external objects into the scene, with no way to preserve the original collections and sub-collections hierarchy, leaving the Outliner cluttered and difficult to manage. Linking also offers an additional advantage: any future updates made to the asset in the source file are automatically reflected in the scene, eliminating the need to re-import.

What are the segdisp_* custom properties on my Pro object?

They are recognition/recovery metadata, not display controls. Leave segdisp_type, segdisp_schema, segdisp_edition and segdisp_modifier intact, and do not manually rename/delete the SegDisp modifier. An object's identity does not always identify its correct empty modifier; ambiguous targets require Needs Review. See recognition properties.

Why are segment value results not shown in solid shading mode when the display base is toggled?

The LED part of the segment display object is a solid mesh aligned over the display base and visible via an emission material, which is not noticeable in solid mode. If you want to see the value results, you may have to switch to the material or rendered view. However, if you are working in a busy scene and don't want to lose viewport performance, you can toggle the "Solid Viewport Preview" button in the "Viewport & Overlays" add-on panel to see the results in solid view. See Viewport & Overlays for details.

Info

The Solid Viewport Preview sets the viewport object color to "Attribute (Vertex)", which affects the entire scene.

Why are there two different options for the Numbers category?

Blender stores number inputs as single-precision floats (float32), which limit the precision of a single input. SegDisp Pro's Simple input supports values up to 10,000,000; an 8-digit display does not mean every 8-digit value is supported.

That's why the Numbers category offers two input options:

  • Simple: A single input field for everyday values, with up to 8 display digits and a maximum input value of 10,000,000.
  • Complex: Builds the current number from five three-digit input groups, each accepting 0-999, for up to 15 display digits. These are not fixed decimal or place-value separator groups. Display Length determines which groups remain active, while Decimals and Decimal Length determine decimal formatting. The rightmost group [1] remains active for whole numbers when Decimals is off.

See the Troubleshooting page for details.

docs.title: Animation & Rendering
docs.text:
Can I animate the display values?

Yes. Most N-panel inputs can be keyframed like any other Blender property: hover over a value and press I. The Time category also includes built-in auto animations (Clock and Timer), so you don't have to keyframe anything for clocks and countdowns. Since Blender can't animate text inputs, the Alphanumeric category uses a built-in multi-input preset system to switch between words over time. See the Alphanumeric page for more details.

Does it render in both Cycles and EEVEE?

Yes, both engines are supported. In EEVEE, enable Raytracing in Properties > Render Properties so the segment emission lights up the scene the way it does in Cycles. More tips are on the Troubleshooting page.

Why is my timer drifting at 29.97 fps?

The auto time animations (Clock, Timer), including Clock Start Frame and Timer Start Frame, only work correctly with whole-number frame rates such as 24, 25, 30, or 60. Decimal frame rates like 23.98 or 29.97 cause small timing errors because of how Blender converts frames to time. Also, make sure the "Addon Frame Rate" dropdown in the N-panel matches your scene's frame rate. See the Preferences & Settings page for details.

docs.title: Sharing & Exporting
docs.text:
Can I link a SegDisp object from another project?

This workflow is not currently validated. Configure and animate displays in their owning project; repair and save that source before reloading its library in the destination. Recovery does not directly edit source-linked modifiers. Lite testing showed input-type errors after library reload; restarting cleared the observed error but is not a guaranteed fix or a confirmed Pro defect. Linked-object still and animation rendering remain unverified. See linking limitations.

Can I share my .blend file with someone who doesn't own the add-on?

Yes, if you share the generated display as an applied or converted mesh rather than redistributing the supplied asset .blend file. Work on a copy if you want to keep the original procedural display editable.

An unapplied SegDisp object still depends on the linked asset file in the add-on installation and may appear as a plane when that file is unavailable. To continue editing it procedurally, your teammate needs their own copy of the matching add-on edition and its assets; Lite cannot control Pro objects. Do not pack or include the supplied asset .blend file as a way to bypass that requirement.

Can I export to Unity, Unreal or FBX?

Yes. Apply the SegDisp object's Geometry Nodes modifier to convert the generated display into a mesh, then export it in a format supported by your target software, such as FBX, for use in Unity, Unreal or other game engines. Work on a copy if you want to retain the original procedural display.

Applying the modifier captures the current geometry; it does not automatically transfer SegDisp's procedural controls or Geometry Nodes-driven animation to another application. Exporting your generated display mesh is allowed. The restriction is on redistributing the supplied asset .blend file, not on exporting SegDisp objects.

docs.title: Alphanumeric
docs.text: Input Capabilities: The Alphanumeric Main Display seamlessly processes inputs containing both numbers and letters, fully supporting both uppercase and lowercase characters, allowing you to mix and match digits and alphabetic characters freely within a single input. Both single and multi input options are available, and the input also supports blank spaces and separator characters.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
[1] Display Count: The alphanumeric category allows you to utilize up to three separate displays simultaneously.

[2] Display Length: The total number of digits shown in a single display.

[3] Input Alignment: You can snap and align your text to either the left or right side of the digital display.

[4] Input Options: Single / Multi

[5] Single Input: Accepts a single text value containing both letters and numbers, including uppercase and lowercase characters, digits, blank spaces, and separator characters.

[6] [7] Preset Selector & Slots: Because Blender does not natively support the animation of string (text) inputs, the add-on includes a built-in multi-input preset system. By switching your input option to "Multi," you can type different words and numbers into a pre-defined list of up to 10 preset slots. You can then keyframe the "Preset Selector" number to animate the text changing over time. Please note that blank spaces and separator characters are not synced between presets. For a realistic result, you will need to configure them manually for each preset.

[8] Preset Focus Mode: Use the two icon buttons beside Preset Selector to choose which preset inputs are visible:

  • Show as List (list icon): Shows all preset inputs for this display.
  • Show Selected (minus icon): Shows only the selected preset input.

docs.title: Alphanumeric Separators (Using Spaces)
docs.text:
[1] [2] Creating Separators: To add a separator character between your data points, simply type a space directly between your inputs in the text field. Do not attempt to enter separator characters (like dots or dashes) directly into the input field, as this will cause an error.

[3] Independent Separator Controls: Each space you type automatically activates a dedicated tab ("Alphanum 1" and "Alphanum 2") in the Separators panel. By default, the first space generates a dot, and the second space generates a comma.

Note: In the separator demo below, Alphanum 2 was changed to a dot, so the BL_EN_DER example shows two dots rather than the default dot and comma.

[4] Simulating True Spaces: If you want an actual blank space rather than a symbol, select "X" from the Separator panel's character menu. This will insert an extra, empty digit to simulate a blank space.

You can enter a maximum of two spaces per display.

If you include more than two spaces, you will trigger an error or the display will appear empty.

Procedural Placement Warning

Because separators are generated procedurally from spaces rather than from direct text input, typing separator characters (such as dots or dashes) directly into the input field will not draw the separators. It will just add a blank space. The add-on exclusively accepts space characters as separator input. You can enter two space characters next to each other.

docs.title: Display Length Behavior
docs.text: When determining your overall "Display Length," remember that typing a space and selecting a separator character will take up exactly one digit of that total length. The same rule applies to the second separator character. To match the exact display length, use blank spaces.

docs.title: Multi-Display Setup
docs.text:
[1] Adding Displays: You can creatively arrange and utilize up to three separate alphanumeric displays (Main Display 1, Display 2, and Display 3) at the same time.

Separators In Between Option:

  • [2] Characters: Separator characters are inserted between each individual character of the text. (Main Display-1 only)
  • [3] Displays: Separator characters are inserted between the additional displays.

[4] Display Separations: You can adjust the physical separation space between the main display and the additional displays using the "Display Separation" value.

Important Separators Limitation

Please note that fully functional separator characters are exclusively available on Main Display-1. If you use spaces in Display 2 or Display 3, they will appear as empty digits rather than actual separator characters. For more complex setups, manually stack additional segment display objects next to each other.

See the Separators page for more information.

docs.title: Simple Number Inputs
docs.text:
[1] Number Input Option:

  • Simple: Up to 8 display digits with a single input. The maximum input value is 10,000,000; an 8-digit display does not mean every 8-digit value is supported. See Troubleshooting: Numbers for details.

  • Complex: Up to 15 display digits using five input groups.

[2] Display Length: The Digit Count.

[3] Decimals allows you to enable or disable decimal values within your digital readouts. Depending on the input category you are using, it serves a few specific purposes:

  • In the Numbers Category: Enabling this option allows you to set an exact "Decimal Count," giving you precise control over the decimal precision of your readout.

  • In the Time Category (Timers): Toggling timer decimals allows for high-precision time tracking. Once enabled, you can set the display to show specific decimal time units, such as centiseconds, deciseconds, or milliseconds.Read more on the Time page.

[4] Decimal Length: This option becomes available when Decimals is enabled. It allows you to specify the number of decimal places to display in your digital readout, providing fine-tuned control over the precision of your numerical data.

Decimal Length cannot equal the main Display Length [2]. An error message will appear if they match.

[5] Place value separation is the system that determines how much each digit in a number is worth based on its position, which is calculated in powers of ten (ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, and so on).

[6] Hide Leading Zeros: A leading zero is a "0" digit preceding the first non-zero digit in a number string. These zeros do not affect the mathematical value of whole numbers, so they can be omitted or hidden without losing information. However, leading zeros are necessary to convey magnitude for numbers after a decimal point and cannot be removed. The "Hide Leading Zeros" toggle in the Segment Display Add-on formats digital readouts by hiding non-value zeros next to numbers.

[7] Left Align: The current number is snapped to the left side of the display. This feature is only available if "decimals" or "place value separation" is disabled.

[8] Minus Sign: Procedurally toggles the minus sign to produce negative numbers.

[9] The current value displayed on the readout.

docs.title: Complex Number Input
docs.text:
Blender uses single-precision floats (float32), which limit the precision of a single number input. SegDisp Pro's Simple input supports values up to 10,000,000. For larger values, use Complex input to build a number from five three-digit input groups, each accepting 0-999, for up to 15 display digits.

The groups control blocks of the current number; they are not fixed decimal or place-value separator groups. Display Length determines which groups remain active, while Decimals and Decimal Length determine decimal formatting. The rightmost group [1] remains active for whole numbers when Decimals is off.

The callouts below refer to the five input fields in the Complex Number UI screenshot, numbered from right to left:

[1] Rightmost input group: Sets the rightmost three-digit block of the current number, from 0-999; it is not reserved for decimals.

[2] Second input group: Sets the next three-digit block to the left of [1], from 0-999.

[3] Third input group: Sets the next three-digit block to the left of [2], from 0-999.

[4] Fourth input group: Sets the next three-digit block to the left of [3], from 0-999.

[5] Leftmost input group: Sets the leftmost three-digit block, from 0-999.

Note: Groups that are not needed for the selected Display Length become inactive. These five callout numbers are separate from the Simple Number Inputs callouts above.

docs.title: General Overview
docs.text:
The Time module allows you to animate digital clocks, countdown timers, and calendar dates without the hassle of complex math or node trees.

Animation Modes: You can fully automate your displays by syncing them directly to your Scene Time, or switch to Manual Keyframing to create stylized, non-linear time animations.

docs.title: Clock
docs.text:
Build realistic digital clocks effortlessly. You can manually input the exact Hour, Minute, and Second, and precisely control the readout by toggling seconds on or off.

[1] Time Categories: Clock, timer and date

[2] Time Format: Choose between standard 12h or 24h clock formats.

[3] Toggle Seconds: Show/Hide second units.

[4] Initial Time: In this example, an initial time of 19:00 is entered. Since 12-hour format is selected, the display shows 07:00.

[5] Clock Direction: You can reverse the flow of time by switching the animation direction between Reverse and Forward.

[6] Auto Time Animation: The clock starts when you hit play in the scene. Clock Start Frame lets you specify the exact frame number at which the animation begins playing back.

[7] Manual Time Animation: You can manually keyframe your animation in non-linear time. The multiplier menu also lets you create high-speed time lapses by scaling your input range — for example, multiplying the speed so that one input second visually represents a full minute or even an hour:

Time Example

If the clock is set to 07:00:00 and the animation slider to 1s: 1 second = [a second]: 07:00:01 1 second = [a minute]: 07:01:00 1 second = [an hour]: 08:00:00

Wrong Results

When setting the time, if you see incorrect results on the display, make sure your scene's animation playhead is set to frame 0 or 1.

Frame Rate Syncing (Important)

Auto time animations only perform properly in sync with whole number frame rates (such as 24, 25, 30, or 60 fps). Fractional frame rates like 29.97 fps will not provide accurate results. Always ensure the add-on frame rate in the "Addon Settings" panel matches your scene frame rate. See the Settings Page for more details.

docs.title: Timer
docs.text:
Perfect for explosive countdowns or intricate chronometers, the Timer feature spans across days, hours, minutes, and seconds.

[1] Whole Timer Units: S: Seconds, M: Minutes, H: Hours, D: Days.

[2] Decimal Timer Units: For high-precision readouts, enable decimal times to display centiseconds, deciseconds, or milliseconds.

[3] Set Timer & Multiplier: Easily set massive durations without doing complex math or trying to enter huge values directly into the "Set Timer" input field. For example, setting the multiplier menu to "Hour" and the input to 24s will automatically calculate the 86,400 seconds needed for a 1-Day countdown.

[4] Timer Count Mode: Set your timer to Countdown (e.g., 3 - 2 - 1 - 0) or Count Up (e.g., 0 - 1 - 2 - 3). If you set your timer to 7 for example, Countdown means the timer will count down from 7 and stop at 0, while Count Up means the timer will start at 0 and stop once it reaches 7.

[5] Auto Timer Animation: The timer starts when you hit play in the scene. "Timer Start Frame" lets you specify the exact frame number at which the animation begins playing back.

[6] Manual Timer Animation & Decimal Precision (Beta): When manually keyframing timer animations, you have full control over decimal precision by choosing between Centiseconds, Deciseconds, or Milliseconds — available when "Timer Decimals" is enabled.

  • High Precision (Milliseconds): Choose this option for ultra-precise, detailed readouts. Because of the high data density, slider adjustments will feel slower and more sensitive.

  • Standard Precision (Centiseconds - Default): The recommended setting for most workflows. It provides faster slider responsiveness and is the optimal choice if you are primarily animating whole-time units (like seconds, minutes, or hours).

True Zero Offset

If you want your timer to start from a true zero time, adjust the Timer Start Frame: set it to 2 if your timeline playhead starts at keyframe 1, or set it to 1 if your playhead starts at keyframe 0.

docs.title: Date
docs.text:
Quickly generate procedural calendar readouts with full formatting control over your display.

[1] Date Format: Customize the exact order of your calendar units (Day, Month, Year) to fit your regional layout.

[2] Year Format: Choose to display the year as either a minimal 2-digit or a full 4-digit readout.

[3] Month Format: You can represent the month as a standard numeric value or select Alphabet for a 3-letter month abbreviation. Note: The alphabetic month format is exclusively available when using the 16-Segment Display Model, due to the segment count limitations of the 7-Segment model.
