docs.title: Installation & Activation
docs.text:
Info

Both editions of Segment Display are distributed as zip-formatted Blender legacy add-ons, not extensions. Install them from the "Add-ons" tab in the Preferences window using the "Install from Disk" option in the top-right dropdown menu.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Before you begin, make sure your system matches the add-on's requirements:

Item Requirement Compatible Blender 5.1 (minimum 5.1.1) Render Engines Eevee, Cycles OS Platforms Windows, Linux, macOS Add-on Format Legacy/zip Script Size 492 – 575 KB Asset Size 170 – 200 MB Internet Connection To activate/deactivate, and at least once every 14 days (see below)

OS Compatibility

The Segment Display add-on was not developed for a specific operating system. However, it has only been tested on a Windows 11 system. Before purchasing the Pro edition, we recommend testing your system with the free Lite edition.

docs.title: Downloading the Add-on
docs.text: Download the Segment Display Pro zip file from your purchase/download location. You will also receive a license key, which is required to unlock the product.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The add-on ships with the asset blend file already included in the zip package. It will be installed automatically into the Blender addons directory when you complete the installation steps below.

Do not unpack the "segment_display_pro_vX.X.X.zip" file

Install the add-on directly from the zip file. Do not extract or rename the files inside it, as this can break the add-on.

docs.title: From the Preferences Panel
docs.text:
1. Open Blender.
  2. Go to Edit → Preferences → Add-ons.
  3. Click the down arrow at the top right and choose "Install from Disk...".
  4. In the file browser, open the settings panel (gear icon, top right). Under "Legacy Add-ons", make sure "Target Path" is set to "Default" and "Overwrite" is ticked.
  5. Select the Segment Display Pro ZIP file, then click "Install from Disk".
  6. Make sure "Segment Display Pro" is enabled (checkbox ticked).
  7. Restart Blender after installation to refresh the asset file.

docs.title: Drag & Drop the ZIP (Optional)
docs.text:
1. You can also install the add-on by dragging its ZIP file directly into Blender instead of opening Preferences first.
  2. Drag the Segment Display Pro ZIP file from your computer’s file manager onto the Blender window. You do not need to drop it in a specific editor or area. Do not extract it first.
  3. In the Install from Disk popup, leave Target set to Default.
  4. Make sure Overwrite and Enable on Install are checked, then click OK.
  5. Check that "Segment Display Pro" is enabled in Edit → Preferences → Add-ons (checkbox ticked).
  6. Restart Blender after installation to refresh the asset file.

Dropping the ZIP doesn't open the install popup? Use Install from Disk... instead.

After enabling, the add-on appears in the 3D Viewport sidebar under the SegDisp Pro tab.

For Lite users

Follow the same steps using the Segment Display Lite ZIP file, then open the SegDisp Lite tab.

Tip for add-on updates

If you have already activated the add-on, drag and drop is a convenient way to install a newer version. Use the new ZIP file and keep Overwrite checked, then restart Blender to refresh the asset file.

Only Blender's default add-on folder is tested

Installing into a custom add-on directory (a custom Target Path or custom Script Directory) may cause problems with using, activating and updating the add-on.

docs.title: Add-on Default File Directory
docs.text:
The add-on and its related asset files will be installed in the same directory (Blender Foundation scripts\addons).

  • WINDOWS:
    • Add-on Script Files: C:\Users\$USER\AppData\Roaming\Blender Foundation\Blender\5.1\scripts\addons
    • Add-on Asset Files: C:\Users\$USER\AppData\Roaming\Blender Foundation\Blender\5.1\scripts\addons\segment-display-pro\assets
  • MacOS: /Users/$USER/Library/Application Support/Blender/5.1/scripts/addons/
  • Linux: ~/.config/blender/5.1/scripts/addons/

Custom Add-on Directory

If you use a custom add-on directory, proper linking of asset files within a scene cannot be guaranteed, even if the add-on uses relative paths to reference assets. This add-on has only been tested with the default Blender scripts directory.

docs.title: Activation/Deactivation
docs.text:
After purchasing Segment Display Pro, you will receive an order confirmation email from Lemon Squeezy containing your license key. You can also find your license key anytime in your Lemon Squeezy account under your order details.

  1. In Edit → Preferences → Add-ons, expand "Segment Display Pro".
  2. Paste your license key into the "License Key" field. (Mouse Right-click to paste does not work — use Ctrl+V instead.)
  3. Click "Activate".
  4. When it shows as activated, you're done. Activation stays active after you restart Blender, update or reinstall the add-on, or move to a newer Blender version.

The status monitor above the key field displays your current activation status (top-left) and your activation limit/seats (top-right).

Click to read this before uninstalling the add-on: Opens a popup explaining why you must deactivate your license before uninstalling.

Internet Connection Required

License activation and deactivation both require an internet connection. Activation validates your license key online, and deactivation contacts the server to free up your activation slot. This ensures your activation count stays accurate and protected. If either fails, make sure "Allow Online Access" is enabled in Blender under Preferences > System > Network.

Working offline (14-day grace period)

Once activated, the add-on re-checks your license with the Lemon Squeezy server when Blender starts. If the server can't be reached (no internet connection, or "Allow Online Access" is turned off), the add-on keeps working for up to 14 days after its last successful check. Every successful check resets the 14-day period.

In the last 3 days, a red warning with the days left (for example "Offline verification: 2 days left") appears at the top of the add-on's N-panel and in the license panel in Preferences. After 14 days without a successful check, the add-on locks and the warning changes to "Offline period expired". Under each warning, "Read more..." explains what happened and what to do, and "Verify now" checks your license online right away. If you're still offline, Verify now tells you that an internet connection is required.

To unlock it, connect to the internet, make sure "Allow Online Access" is enabled, and click "Verify now". The add-on also checks again on its own within about 2 minutes, or when you restart Blender. Your license is confirmed again and the 14-day period starts over. This does not use a new activation seat.

Setting your computer's clock back also locks the add-on ("System clock was moved back"). Set the correct date and time, go online, then click "Verify now".

If you usually work offline, go online and open Blender at least once every 14 days to keep the add-on unlocked.

docs.title: The License File
docs.text:
Your activation is saved in a small license file (sdp_activation.lic) outside the add-on folder, so updating or reinstalling the add-on doesn't affect it:

  • Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\OrionNovember.Studio\SegmentDisplay_Pro\
  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/OrionNovember.Studio/SegmentDisplay_Pro/
  • Linux: ~/.local/state/OrionNovember.Studio/SegmentDisplay_Pro/ (or $XDG_STATE_HOME/OrionNovember.Studio/SegmentDisplay_Pro/ if set)

For Lite users

Lite saves its activation in sdl_activation.lic, in its own folder:

  • Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\OrionNovember.Studio\SegmentDisplay_Lite\
  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/OrionNovember.Studio/SegmentDisplay_Lite/
  • Linux: ~/.local/state/OrionNovember.Studio/SegmentDisplay_Lite/ (or $XDG_STATE_HOME/OrionNovember.Studio/SegmentDisplay_Lite/ if set)

The same rules below apply to the Lite file.

Do not edit, move or copy the license file

Don't edit or move this file, and don't copy it to another computer. The license file is tied to the computer it was activated on, so a copied file will not unlock the add-on on any other machine. Every new or additional computer must be activated on its own by entering your license key in the add-on preferences, and each activation uses one seat of your activation limit. Deleting the file does NOT free up an activation slot. Use "Deactivate" in the add-on or your Lemon Squeezy order dashboard instead.

docs.title: Activation Limit
docs.text:
Activation limits per license key: Pro: 3 activation seats; Lite: 1 activation seat. Every new device counts toward the limit for your edition.

Moving to a new computer?

Deactivate the license on the old machine first. Uninstalling the add-on without deactivating does NOT free up the activation slot. Lost access to the old machine? You can deactivate it yourself from your Lemon Squeezy order dashboard, where you can also see and manage all your activations.

Reinstalling your operating system?

Reinstalling your operating system counts as a new computer. The add-on will ask you to activate again, and the old activation keeps its slot until you remove it from your Lemon Squeezy order dashboard.

Privacy Notice

During license activation, your custom device name (e.g., SDPRO-QUEEN-WINDOWS11) is stored on our online system dashboard. This information is used exclusively by our customer support to assist you in the event of any activation issues. By activating your license, you consent to sharing this device identifier with us.

Device name on the dashboard

The device name on your Lemon Squeezy order dashboard is your computer's name at the time you first activated. Renaming the computer later doesn't change it there, and doesn't use a new activation. Want the new name to show? Click "Deactivate", then "Activate" again. This frees the old slot and takes a new one, so your activation count stays the same.

docs.title: Updating the Add-on
docs.text:
Pro v1.0.1 and later

  1. Save a backup copy of your project before updating or repairing connections.
  2. Install the complete new ZIP over the existing add-on with Target Path: Default and Overwrite enabled. No uninstall is needed. Dragging the new ZIP into Blender also works (see Drag & Drop the ZIP). Your activation file is outside the add-on folder, so reinstalling does not normally require reactivation.
  3. Restart Blender, reopen your project and inspect the displays, settings and animation. Reinstalling and restarting often restores displays automatically; if everything is correct, no manual recovery is needed.
  4. If Asset Status shows Not Available, reinstall the matching complete package to restore the shipped asset in the add-on's assets folder, then restart again. Do not delete modifiers or remove node-tree assignments to fix this state.
  5. If supported connection issues remain while the installed asset is available, open Edit > Preferences > Add-ons > Segment Display Pro > Asset Status > Review & Recover…. Review the proposed actions, recover, inspect the result and save the project. See the recovery walkthrough.

Reconnection uses settings and animation still present in your project. It cannot restore data already deleted by removing a modifier or node-tree assignment. Lite recovery differs and is not covered in this Pro manual.

Changing Blender versions

Blender keeps installations in version-specific folders, so changing Blender versions can change asset paths. Install a matching, supported package in the target Blender version and restart before checking the project. Recovery is not a guarantee of compatibility with an untested Blender version.

Custom add-on directories are not tested

If you installed the add-on into a custom Target Path or Script Directory, updating may not work properly. Use the default add-on folder.

docs.title: Uninstalling
docs.text:
Always deactivate your license before uninstalling the add-on

If you remove the add-on without deactivating first, the device will still count toward your activation limit. Unfortunately, Blender does not allow add-ons to prevent or intercept the uninstall action. If you accidentally uninstall without deactivating, you can manage your activation seats yourself by logging into the Lemon Squeezy customer portal with your purchase email. Under your order's license key details, you can view all active devices and deactivate any instance to free up a seat. If you need help with this, please reach out to our support email for guidance.

Accidentally Uninstalled the Add-on Mid-Project?

Displays can appear as planes because the linked asset is unavailable; this does not by itself mean their stored settings are lost. Preserve the project and leave its modifiers untouched. Reinstall the complete matching add-on, restart Blender and check the project first. Displays often return without manual recovery. If supported issues remain, use Pro Review & Recover… once the asset is available. Inspect settings and animation before saving; deleted data cannot be guaranteed recoverable. See Review & Recover.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Segment Display Pro is a procedural Blender add-on that lets you create fully customizable segment displays using Geometry Nodes. Inspired by the real electronic components found in digital clocks, calculators, speedometers, and control panels, it brings that distinct segmented aesthetic into your 3D and motion graphics projects without the hassle of manual modeling. All controls are exposed through a clean N-panel interface in the 3D View sidebar, so you can build and drive segment-style readings without leaving the viewport.

This manual covers everything you need to get started: installation, activation, the N-panel interface, and a detailed breakdown of every input and setting available to you. Whether you're building a retro dashboard or a sci-fi HUD, this guide will help you get the most out of the add-on.

Note for Lite edition users:

The Segment Display Lite edition does not have a separate user manual. However, Lite users can still reference this manual for the Installation, Activation, Troubleshooting, and Settings & Preferences sections, as they apply to both editions. Exception: Lite's asset recovery procedure differs from Pro's and is not covered in this manual. The remaining sections (such as Input Categories) cover Pro-specific features, but may still be useful as a general reference.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Segment Display Pro provides a set of display modules that you place and control from the N-panel. The available areas include:

  • Numbers — numeric segment readouts.
  • Alphanumeric — text and character displays.
  • Time — clock, timer and date readouts.
  • Separators — whole and decimal separator elements for composing layouts.
  • Display Options — organize and switch between display groups.
  • Viewport overlays — on-screen visual aids while working.
  • Add-on settings — global preferences and options.

Each module is driven by the same underlying Geometry Nodes assets, so the display geometry stays procedural and adjustable after creation.

docs.title: Add-on Credits & Requirements
docs.text:
Item Requirement Full Name Segment Display Pro N-panel Label SegDisp Pro Add-on Version 1.0.1 Assets Version 1.0.1 (must match the add-on version) Compatible Blender 5.1 (Minimum 5.1.1)¹ Developer Orion November Studio Render Engines Eevee, Cycles OS Platforms Windows², Linux, macOS Location in UI 3D View → Sidebar (N) → SegDisp Pro tab Add-on Type/Format Legacy/zip Script Size 492 – 575 KB³ Asset Size 170 – 200 MB³

Important

¹ 5.1.1 is the minimum Blender version the add-on declares. SegDisp v1.0.1 has been tested with Blender 5.1.2, the recommended version for this release, but has not yet been re-tested on 5.1.1. Newer Blender versions are not confirmed as supported yet.

² The Segment Display add-on was not developed for a specific operating system. However, it has only been tested on a Windows 11 system. Before purchasing the Pro edition, we recommend testing your system with the free Lite edition.

³ File sizes may change over time with future updates.

v1.0.1 and later

To see the versions installed on your computer, open About in the add-on preferences or at the bottom of the N-panel. See Add-on Credits.

docs.title: Where to find it in Blender
docs.text: After the add-on is enabled, open the 3D Viewport and press N to show the sidebar. Segment Display Pro appears under its own SegDisp Pro tab, alongside Blender's other N-panel categories.

docs.title: The Asset File
docs.text:
When you add a display, its Geometry Nodes setup uses the .blend asset linked from the add-on's assets folder. Displays can share this library, including across scenes. If the asset is missing or its path changes, displays may appear as planes without their stored modifier settings being lost.

Pro v1.0.1 and later

Preserve a project copy, reinstall the complete matching add-on and restart Blender first. Displays often reconnect automatically; if they are correct, no manual recovery is needed. If supported problems remain, use Preferences > Add-ons > Segment Display Pro > Asset Status > Review & Recover…. Reconnecting a library retains data still present; restoring an empty node-tree assignment and recreating a deleted modifier are different operations. Recreation uses defaults, not deleted settings or animation. See Review & Recover.

Protect your project and shipped asset

Do not delete the linked library, remove node-tree assignments or rename/delete display modifiers as a repair shortcut. Recovery cannot guarantee restoration of missing settings or animation. Each edition controls its own objects; Pro recovery does not convert Lite objects.

Do not open, modify, re-save, rename or move the shipped asset file. Re-saving changes its byte-level fingerprint even if it looks unchanged. Reinstall the original ZIP if it was altered. See asset safety and recovery limits.

Why this matters for support: OrionNovember.Studio cannot provide support for modified asset files. Opening and re-saving the shipped asset changes its digital fingerprint, even if you make no visible changes. If the asset has been modified, reinstall the complete add-on from the original ZIP before requesting support.

docs.title: The Segment Display Object
docs.text:
• The "Add Segment Display" button in the N-panel interface only appears when you click on an empty space in the 3D scene. The object is always added at the current 3D cursor location.

  • If you add a SegDisp object while the viewport is in Solid shading mode, you may not see the results of your inputs. Switch to Material Preview or Rendered shading, enable Solid Viewport Preview in the Viewport & Overlays panel, or disable/hide the LED Base to make the segment values visible. See Troubleshooting: Viewport | Solid Color Preview for Solid viewport limitations and fixes.

  • The N-panel always displays the settings of the active segment display object (the one with the brighter outline, i.e. the last one you clicked). You don't need it to be the only selected object; even if multiple objects are selected, the panel controls whichever segment display is active.

  • The object settings will only appear if a Segment Display object is active or selected. If any other type of element is selected in the scene, a "Select a Segment Display object" message will be shown instead.

Important

Each edition can only control objects created with that edition. SegDisp Pro cannot control SegDisp Lite objects, and SegDisp Lite cannot control SegDisp Pro objects. Use the matching add-on's N-panel to adjust each object.

docs.title: Licensing
docs.text: Segment Display Pro is a commercial add-on. It uses license-key activation, so a valid key is required to unlock the full feature set. See the installation and Activation pages for details.

docs.title: Preferences & Settings
docs.text: The Settings & Preferences panel is where you manage your license activation and monitor the health of your linked asset files. Access it via Edit > Preferences > Add-ons, then expand the Segment Display Pro entry.

docs.title: License Activation Panel
docs.text:
The License Activation section displays your current activation status and allows you to manage your license key.

License notice: In the last 3 days of the offline grace period (e.g. "Offline verification: 2 days left") or when the add-on is locked (e.g. "Offline period expired"), a red message appears at the top of this section. The same notice also appears at the top of the add-on's N-panel. See the Activation page for details. Read more...: Opens a popup with the full explanation and the steps to fix it. Verify now: Checks your license online right away and shows the result: "License Verified", "No Internet Connection" or "Verification Failed". Verifying never uses another activation seat. See Verify now results.

Status: Shows whether your license is currently activated or not (checkmark icon when active). When the add-on is locked, it shows "Not Activated" and the reason appears in the red license notice above it. Other problems, for example "Activation belongs to another computer", are shown here. Activations: Displays how many device slots you've used out of your total allowance. Pro: 3 activation seats; Lite: 1 activation seat (e.g. 1/3 for Pro or 1/1 for Lite). The count is refreshed by the online check, so it shows "(last known)" when the add-on is locked or the offline grace period is almost over.

License Key: The masked key field where you enter or view your license key. Activate: Activates your license key on this device. If this device was activated before, its existing seat is reused instead of taking a new one. Deactivate: Removes the license activation from the current device, freeing up a slot for use on another machine.

Click to read this before uninstalling the add-on: Opens a popup explaining why you must deactivate your license before uninstalling.

Warning

Always deactivate your license before uninstalling the add-on. If you skip this step, the device will still count toward your activation limit. See the Activation page for more details.

docs.title: Review & Recover
docs.text:
Pro v1.0.1 and later

Your displays use a linked asset file supplied with the add-on. Review & Recover… checks supported connections and lets you review repairs before applying them. Open Edit > Preferences > Add-ons > Segment Display Pro > Asset Status.

Available means the installed asset file can be found, not that every display in your project is connected correctly. A separate message can report displays needing re-linking or toggle inputs needing repair. The asset name and Asset Version identify the installed asset.

Lite users: Lite uses a different, simplified Re-link operation. Its recovery procedure is not covered in this Pro manual. Pro recovery does not convert Lite objects into Pro objects.

docs.title: Before you recover
docs.text:
Save a copy of your project. If displays appear as planes after an update or reinstall, restart Blender and reopen the project first. Reinstalling the complete matching add-on and restarting usually restored displays automatically in testing. If the displays, settings and animation are correct, no manual recovery is needed.

If Asset Status reports Not Available, follow the missing-asset steps before attempting recovery. Do not delete modifiers, remove node-tree assignments or edit recognition properties to repair a missing asset connection.

docs.title: Restore Node Tree
docs.text:
This section restores the asset-tree assignment on an existing, identified modifier. Review the listed object, scene and modifier before leaving it selected.

Deleted settings and animation are not restored

Assigning the tree again cannot restore input settings or animation already deleted when you removed the node tree from the Geometry Nodes panel. By contrast, removing the asset through Outliner > Blender File can leave settings that recovery can retain. Recovery depends on the data still present; do not deliberately delete the asset as a repair step.

In v1.0.1, Restore Node Tree does not display the deleted-settings warning in the dialog. Its absence is not a promise that deleted data can be recovered.

docs.title: Recreate Missing Modifier (Defaults)
docs.text:
If a recognized, supported Pro object has no Geometry Nodes modifier, recovery can offer to create one. This option is unchecked by default. Select it only when you want a replacement using defaults.

The new modifier is added at the end of the stack. Deleted input settings, animation and the original modifier-stack position are not restored. Not every object with a missing modifier qualifies for recreation.

docs.title: Needs Review
docs.text:
These entries are unchecked by default because recovery cannot confidently choose the target. Select only a display you recognize, then choose its correct empty Geometry Nodes modifier from the dropdown.

segdisp_pro.002 selected here after review.

The object's segdisp_* properties can identify it as a Pro display without identifying which empty modifier belongs to it. Recovery also checks the remembered modifier name in segdisp_modifier. If that name no longer matches, or the target is ambiguous, a generic name such as GeometryNodes or GeometryNodes.001 is not enough to choose safely. A generic name does not always require review: an exact remembered match can still identify the correct modifier.

Do not rename or delete the SegDisp modifier or change its recognition properties manually. If you cannot identify the correct modifier, leave the entry unchecked. A name-based candidate is not proof that an object belongs to SegDisp.

docs.title: Reconnect Asset Library
docs.text:
Use this section when a supported project library link is broken or points to an asset outside the current installation. Check the stored path, installed target and affected displays, then review Reconnect this library.

Reconnecting a library affects every display using it, in every scene. When the original modifiers and stored settings/animation remain intact, reconnecting restores the displays using that retained data.

Blender may temporarily stop responding while relocating and reloading linked asset data, particularly for paths outside the current installation. Allow it to finish; a temporary not-responding message does not necessarily mean Blender has crashed. Duration varies.

docs.title: Other results
docs.text:
• Will Fix: Toggle Inputs: Repairs supported Boolean inputs stored as numbers while preserving their on/off values.
  • Not Changed: Reports unsupported or excluded items, such as other-edition objects, local asset-tree copies, unknown asset sources, non-editable or source-linked objects, and missing modifiers that do not qualify for recreation. Recovery does not directly edit source-linked modifiers; repair and save the owning project instead.

Only sections relevant to your project appear. Recovery can be unavailable if the license is inactive, the installed asset is missing or there is nothing supported to recover.

docs.title: Backup, recover and save
docs.text:
1. Review the selected actions. Leave uncertain entries unchecked.
  2. Keep Save a backup copy to your current project location first enabled when possible. A backup requires a project already saved to disk; an unsaved project shows File not saved yet, no backup copy possible. Save it first if you want a backup.
  3. Click Recover. If a requested backup fails, recovery cancels without making changes.
  4. Read the result, including skipped/failed repairs or settings that could not be restored. Inspect the displays, settings and animation.
  5. Save your project to retain successful repairs. Creating a backup does not save the repaired project automatically.

docs.title: Asset Not Available
docs.text:
If your displays appear as planes and you see these messages, do not panic or try to fix the Modifiers panel. The installed asset may be missing, damaged or outside the expected add-on assets location. This does not by itself mean your stored display settings are lost.

  1. Preserve a project copy and leave existing modifiers, node-tree assignments and recognition properties untouched.
  2. Reinstall the complete matching Pro ZIP with the shipped asset included, then restart Blender and reopen the project.
  3. Check the displays first. Reinstalling and restarting is often sufficient; if they are restored correctly, no recovery operation is needed.
  4. If supported connection problems remain, use Review & Recover… once the installed asset is available. Inspect the result and save.

The recovery button can remain disabled until the installed asset is available. Reconnection preserves data still present; it cannot restore deleted settings or animation. See Troubleshooting for related issues.

docs.title: Linked Asset
docs.text: You can inspect the linked library in Outliner > Blender File. Do not remove it as a cleanup or recovery shortcut. Do not open, modify, re-save, rename or move the shipped asset file; reinstall the original ZIP if it was altered.

docs.title: Resources & Support Panel
docs.text:
The Resources & Support box in the add-on preferences collects quick links to help and account pages. Each link opens in your web browser unless noted otherwise.

  • Documentation Home: Opens this manual.
  • Activation/Deactivation: Opens the activation steps.
  • Get Started: Opens the Introduction.
  • User Guide: Opens the Input Categories pages, starting with Numbers.
  • Troubleshooting: Opens the Troubleshooting page.
  • Orion November Studio: Opens the studio website.
  • SegDisp Pro Overview Video: Opens the add-on overview video on YouTube.
  • Email Support: Pro v1.0.1 and later. Opens your default email app with a new message to support@orionnovemberstudio.com. If nothing opens, your computer has no default email app set up; send your message to that address from any email account.
  • Manage My Orders: Opens your Lemon Squeezy order dashboard, where you can find your license key and manage your activations.

Contacting support

Include your Blender version, operating system and add-on version (shown in About) so we can help you faster.

docs.title: About Panel
docs.text:
v1.0.1 and later

About shows your installed product information and update-check results. Open Edit > Preferences > Add-ons > Segment Display Pro > About, or expand About at the bottom of the SegDisp Pro N-panel. The N-panel section starts collapsed; the Preferences section is not collapsible. If the N-panel hides About while an unrelated object is selected, deselect it or use Preferences.

docs.title: Add-on Credits
docs.text:
The v1.0.1 interface labels this group Add-on Credits.

  • Add-on Version: The version of the code currently running in Blender.
  • Assets Version: The version reported by the installed asset file. Unknown means its version information is unavailable, not that the asset is current.
  • Compatible Blender: The add-on's declared minimum Blender version, not a list of every tested or recommended version. See Requirements.
  • Developer: The product's developer credit.

The add-on and asset versions must match. If you see Doesn’t match add-on version or Restart Blender to finish updating to…, restart Blender first: replacing installed files does not immediately replace code already loaded in memory. If a mismatch remains after restarting, reinstall the complete matching Pro ZIP. Do not mix script and asset files from different versions or editions. A known mismatch can block adding a display; Unknown is not confirmation that the versions match.

docs.title: Add-on Update
docs.text:
Click Check for Updates to request a check. The add-on also checks automatically at startup; opening About does not itself start another check.

  • Checking… / Checking for updates...: A request is running. Wait for it to finish; repeat checks are disabled while it runs.
  • You're using the latest version.: The check found no newer release.
  • Update available: v…: A newer release was found. Check for Updates is disabled while a confirmed downloadable update is already available; use Open Downloads instead.
  • Couldn't check for updates. Try again.: The request failed. Check your connection and Blender online-access permission, then retry. A previous successful result may remain visible as Previous result; it is not a fresh check.

Open Downloads opens the release download page in your browser; it does not download or install the add-on or restart Blender. An activated license is required to use this button. If a Before you update dialog appears, read its release notice before continuing. Install the downloaded ZIP yourself and restart Blender. See Updating the Add-on.

Update checks require internet access and Preferences > System > Network > Allow Online Access. If Blender was launched with --offline-mode, restart without that flag before checking again.

docs.title: N-panel update notifications
docs.text:
An automatic check can show Update Available at the top of the N-panel, with the installed and latest versions. Open Downloads opens the release page, the same as in About. Dismiss asks whether to hide these header notices. You can change the same preference under Edit > Preferences > Add-ons > Segment Display Pro > N-panel Options > Hide "Update Available" Notifications on the N-Panel Header.

This hides only the N-panel header update notice. Update information remains available in About and Preferences; license and asset-status warnings are not hidden.

The notification preference is saved in addon_userpref.json beside the activation file, outside the installed add-on folder, so it can survive normal updates and reinstalls. In v1.0.1, this file stores only the header update-notice preference, not all add-on preferences or per-object display settings. Change it through Blender rather than editing the file manually. See The License File for the Pro storage directory; the preference file is separate from the activation file and does not activate the add-on.

docs.title: Time Synchronization
docs.text:
Time Synchronization syncs the Clock and Timer display values to Blender's timeline, matching the add-on's FPS with the scene FPS so the displayed time updates accurately as the animation plays. Set the FPS using the Addon Frame Rate dropdown menu in Addon Settings to match your project's frame rate.

The Clock Start Frame and Timer Start Frame options set the starting frame for their respective auto animations. Their timing depends on the scene FPS and the add-on's internal FPS. See the Input Categories/ Time Page for more details.

Info

These options only work correctly with whole-number frame rates (e.g., 24, 25, 30, 60). Decimal frame rates such as 23.98 or 29.97 will produce slightly inaccurate results due to mathematical limitations.

Addon FPS

Scene FPS

docs.title: Separators
docs.text: Separators are the characters placed between digits or display groups, such as colons, dots, dashes, and other shapes. In real-world electronics, these are commonly seen as the blinking colon on a digital clock or the decimal point on a calculator. SegDisp Pro gives you full control over which separator characters to use, their shape and style, and precisely where they sit relative to your digits. This section covers all separator-related inputs across five panels: Alphanumeric settings, Characters & Shapes, Styles, Position/Spacing/Size, and Decimal-specific options.

docs.title: General Separator Options
docs.text:
[1] Separators tab: Select which separator to edit. Use this tab to switch between the different separators available in your display, allowing you to configure each one individually.

[2] Characters: Selects which character is used as the separator between digits (e.g., colon, dot, dash, slash).

[3] Shape: Selects the geometric shape used as a separator character (e.g., circle, diamond, triangle, square).

Each character and shape has its own dedicated settings and properties. These options appear on the UI depending on your selection:

  • Diamond Variation: Cycles through diamond shape variations when diamond is selected as the separator shape.
  • Triangle Direction: Sets the pointing direction of the triangle separator character.
  • Triangle Tip Align: Adjusts the alignment of the triangle's tip relative to the display.
  • Slash / Line: Switches between a slash, backslash, or straight line as the separator character.
  • Dash Thickness: Controls the thickness of the dash separator character.
  • Dash Length: Controls the length of the dash separator character.
  • Colon Distance: Adjusts the vertical spacing between the two dots of the colon separator.

[4] Shape Corners: Toggles between sharp or rounded corners on the separator character shapes. Round Style: Selects the rounding style applied to dash or slash/line rectangle-shaped characters.

[5] Character Angle: Switches the separator character between Straight and Shear. Note: Not available for slash and line characters.

[6] Vertical Position: Sets the separator's vertical alignment. The character can be automatically aligned to the decimal digit position or manually adjusted to your preference. Decimal digit position options can be found on the Display page.

[7] Custom Vertical Position: Provides a custom vertical position value when automatic alignment is not selected. Manual Vertical Offset: Manually adjusts the vertical offset of the separator character.

[8] Horizontal Position: Sets the separator's horizontal alignment. Can be centered automatically within the digit spaces or offset based on your preferred value. Manual Horizontal Offset: Applies a manual horizontal offset to fine-tune the separator's left/right placement.

[9] Separator Size: Scales the overall size of the separator character. Note: Not available for dash, slash, and line characters since they have their own dedicated size settings.

[10] Size Link to Decimal / Manual: Only on the Decimal Number tab. "Size Link to Decimal" links the separator size to the decimal digit size; "Manual" lets you set it yourself. Decimal digit size options can be found on the Display page.

[11] Separation Space: Controls the spacing for the selected separator. The decimal separator has its own space control. In the Alphanumeric category, use First Separation Space and Second Separation Space for the two separators.

docs.title: Alphanumeric Specific Separator Options
docs.text:
Separators In Between Option:

[1] Characters: Separator characters are inserted between each individual character of the text. (Main Display-1 only)

[2] Displays: Separator characters are inserted between the additional displays.

[3] Display Separations: You can adjust the physical separation space between the main display and the additional displays using the "Display Separation" value.

See the Alphanumeric Input page for more information.

docs.title: Digit-Specific Separator Character
docs.text:
[1] Display Models: Selects the segment display model used for the separator's digit characters.

[2] Display Styles: Selects a visual style preset for the digit separator characters.¹

¹ Info

There is only a single style currently available. The remaining styles are still under development and will be included in future versions.

[3] Segment Count: Sets the number of segments used for the segment variation presets.

[4] Segment Vari: Selects which segment variation preset the separator's digit character uses.

[5] Style Options: Fine-tunes the look of the separator's digit character in the "Whole Sep. | Style Options" panel:

  • Regular / Bold: Sets the pre-defined thickness of the individual segments used in the separator display.

  • 1 – 4: Adjusts the gap between individual segments within the separator's digit characters.

docs.title: Non-character Option
docs.text: If none of the characters are selected, the separations remain, and the spacing can still be adjusted.

docs.title: The Asset File
docs.text:
Displays use the .blend asset linked from the add-on's assets folder. Multiple displays, including those in other scenes, can share the same library. Do not delete that library from Outliner > Blender File as a repair or cleanup shortcut. Only purge unused data after you no longer need the displays and their dependencies.

Pro v1.0.1 and later

docs.title: Displays appear as planes / Asset Not Available
docs.text:
Do not panic or edit the Modifiers panel. Planes after launch, together with Not Available, Asset file info not loaded and Asset Version: Unknown, can mean the installed asset is missing, damaged or outside its expected location. The messages do not by themselves mean your stored settings are lost.

  1. Preserve a project copy; leave modifiers, node-tree assignments and recognition properties untouched.
  2. Reinstall the complete matching Pro ZIP and restart Blender.
  3. Reopen and inspect the project. Displays often return automatically; if they are correct, no recovery operation is needed.
  4. If supported connection issues remain, use Preferences > Add-ons > Segment Display Pro > Asset Status > Review & Recover… once the installed asset is available. Review repairs, inspect the result and save.

The recovery button may be disabled while the installed asset is unavailable. Available only confirms the installed asset can be found, not that every project connection is healthy. For Unknown version information or known asset/add-on version mismatches, restart after updating first; if the issue persists, reinstall the complete matching package. A known mismatch can block Add Segment Display. Do not mix asset/script versions, edit the asset or change licensing to bypass the check.

In About, these cases appear as Doesn’t match add-on version next to Assets Version, or Restart Blender to finish updating to… after installing an update while Blender is running. See Add-on Credits.

docs.title: Recovery limits and lost settings
docs.text:
Reconnecting a library restores displays using settings and animation still present. Restore Node Tree assigns the tree to an existing supported modifier; it cannot restore settings or animation already deleted by removing the assignment in the Geometry Nodes panel. Removing the asset through Outliner > Blender File can leave recoverable settings, but is not a recommended repair method.

Recreate Missing Modifier (Defaults) is opt-in and adds a new modifier at the end of the stack. It does not restore deleted settings, animation or the original stack position. In v1.0.1, the deleted-settings warning is not yet shown under Restore Node Tree; its absence does not guarantee recovery. See the full walkthrough.

docs.title: Blender temporarily stops responding
docs.text: Blender may pause while recovery relocates and reloads an asset library pointing outside the current installation. Allow it to finish; a temporary not-responding message does not necessarily mean a crash. Duration varies. This operation involves Blender's library handling, not solely add-on processing; its precise bottleneck and whether pauses are limited to relocation have not been established.

docs.title: Asset safety
docs.text:
Do not open or modify the asset file!

Do not open, modify, re-save, rename or move the shipped .blend asset. Re-saving changes its byte-level fingerprint even if it looks unchanged. Reinstall the original complete ZIP if the file was altered. This is asset-safety guidance, not a claim that installed files are read-only or that an in-add-on runtime hash check protects them.

Why this matters for support: OrionNovember.Studio cannot provide support for modified asset files. Opening and re-saving the shipped asset changes its digital fingerprint, even if you make no visible changes. If the asset has been modified, reinstall the complete add-on from the original ZIP before requesting support.

Lite users: Lite recovery differs and is not covered in this Pro manual.

docs.title: The Segment Display Object
docs.text:
The "Add Segment Display" button in the N-panel interface only appears when you click on an empty space in the 3D scene. The object is always added at the current 3D cursor location.

The N-panel always displays the settings of the active segment display object (the one with the brighter outline, i.e. the last one you clicked). You don't need it to be the only selected object; even if multiple objects are selected, the panel controls whichever segment display is active.

The object settings will only appear if a Segment Display object is active or selected. If any other type of element is selected in the scene, a "Select a Segment Display object" message will be shown instead.

Important

Each edition can only control objects created with that edition. SegDisp Pro cannot control SegDisp Lite objects, and SegDisp Lite cannot control SegDisp Pro objects. Use the matching add-on's N-panel to adjust each object.

docs.title: Pro recognition properties and modifiers
docs.text:
Local Pro objects can contain segdisp_type, segdisp_schema, segdisp_edition and segdisp_modifier. These are recognition/recovery metadata, not display inputs or the asset file's fingerprint. Do not change/delete them or manually rename/delete the display modifier.

Where to review these IDs: Select the SegDisp Pro object in the 3D Viewport, press N to open the sidebar, then open Item > Properties to inspect its segdisp_* custom properties. Review them without changing or deleting their values.

Why these IDs matter: Review & Recover uses these properties to recognize a SegDisp Pro object and help determine which repairs are safe, especially when its asset-tree assignment or modifier is missing. segdisp_type and segdisp_edition identify the object as a Pro display, segdisp_schema records the recognition-data format, and segdisp_modifier remembers the display modifier's name. Changing or deleting them can prevent confident identification, send an object to Needs Review, or make supported recovery unavailable. They do not store a backup of your input settings or animation, so keeping them intact does not restore data that has already been deleted.

An object can be recognized while its empty modifier remains ambiguous. Names such as GeometryNodes are not proof of a SegDisp modifier. If the remembered modifier name no longer matches, select the correct target only if you recognize it in Needs Review; otherwise leave it unchecked. An exact remembered match can still identify a generically named modifier. See Needs Review.

docs.title: Linking displays from another project
docs.text:
Linking SegDisp objects from another project is not currently a validated workflow. Configure and animate displays in their owning project. Changes saved there do not live-update an already open destination; reload the source library after repairing and saving the source.

Lite testing showed modifier input-type errors after a source-library reload (Property type does not match input socket, for example on Show Separator Origin Point). Restarting Blender cleared the observed error, but is not a guaranteed fix or a confirmed Pro defect. Neither still nor animated rendering through this nested-link workflow has been validated. Recovery does not directly edit source-linked modifiers, although reconnecting a shared asset library can affect linked displays visually.

docs.title: Licensing
docs.text:
Activation limits per license key: Pro: 3 activation seats; Lite: 1 activation seat.

Segment Display Pro is a commercial add-on. It uses license-key activation, so a valid key is required to unlock the full feature set. See the Activation Page for details.

docs.title: License Deactivation Before Uninstall
docs.text:
Always deactivate your license before uninstalling the add-on.

If you remove the add-on without deactivating first, the device will still count toward your activation limit. Unfortunately, Blender's API does not allow add-ons to prevent or intercept the uninstall action, so the add-on cannot warn you or auto-deactivate at that point. If you accidentally uninstall without deactivating, you can free up the slot yourself from your Lemon Squeezy order dashboard. If you need help with this, please contact us via our support email.

License activation and deactivation both require an internet connection.

Activation validates your license key online, and deactivation contacts the server to free up your activation slot. This ensures your activation count stays accurate and protected. If either fails, make sure "Allow Online Access" is enabled in Blender under Preferences > System > Network.

docs.title: License Locked Messages
docs.text:
When the add-on is locked, a red message appears at the top of the N-panel and in the license panel in Preferences, with Read more... and Verify now buttons below it. The Status line shows "Not Activated". None of these use a new activation seat.

Message What it means What to do Offline period expired The license couldn't be checked online for 14 days. Go online, make sure "Allow Online Access" is enabled, and click Verify now. The add-on also unlocks on its own within about 2 minutes, or after a Blender restart. System clock was moved back Your computer's clock is earlier than the last license check or the last time the add-on was used. Correct your system date and time, go online, then click Verify now. License not verified online The license couldn't be confirmed online. Go online, make sure "Allow Online Access" is enabled, and click Verify now. Activation belongs to another computer (Status line) The activation was copied from a different computer. Activate with your license key on this computer. Each computer needs its own activation.

docs.title: Verify now results
docs.text:
After you click Verify now, the add-on checks your license online and shows one of these popups:

Popup What it means License Verified Your license was confirmed online. The add-on is active again and the 14-day offline period starts over. No Internet Connection The license server couldn't be reached. Check your internet connection and make sure "Allow Online Access" is enabled in Preferences > System > Network, then try again. Verification Failed The server rejected the activation (for example, the device was removed from your Lemon Squeezy order dashboard) or didn't answer in time. Try again, or activate again with your license key.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
Blender uses single-precision floating point (float32) internally, which limits the precision of a single number input. SegDisp Pro's Simple input supports values up to 10,000,000. Its 8-digit display length is not a promise that every 8-digit value is supported; use Complex input for larger values rather than relying on rounded results.

Complex input splits the current number into five three-digit input groups, each accepting 0-999, for up to 15 display digits. These groups are not fixed decimal or place-value separator groups: Display Length controls which groups are active, and Decimal Length controls decimal formatting. Group [1] also remains active for whole numbers when Decimals is off. See the Numbers Page for details.

docs.title: Alphanumeric Preset Animations (Multi-Input)
docs.text: Bypassing Blender's Limits: Because Blender does not natively support the animation of string (text) inputs, the add-on includes a built-in multi-input preset system. See the Alphanumeric Input Page for details.

docs.title: Time FPS
docs.text:
The auto time animations (Clock, Timer), including Clock Start Frame and Timer Start Frame, only work correctly with whole-number frame rates (e.g. 24, 25, 30, 60). Decimal frame rates such as 23.98 or 29.97 will produce slightly inaccurate timing results due to mathematical limitations in how Blender calculates frame-to-time conversions.

Make sure the Addon Frame Rate dropdown in the add-on's N-panel settings matches your project's scene frame rate for accurate time synchronization. For more information, see the Settings Page.

docs.title: Viewport | Solid Color Preview
docs.text:
The Solid Viewport Preview feature may not display correctly in certain conditions: With some of the Matcap lighting methods in the 3D Viewport's solid shading mode. If Snap Guides are enabled (this is handled internally with a state toggle).

If your Segment Display object looks glitchy from a distance when Solid Viewport Preview is enabled, increase the Clip Start value (near clipping distance) in the Blender N-Panel View options. The add-on also makes a slight adjustment to the LED Base to prevent this geometry face clipping issue. The temporary LED Base adjustment applies exclusively to the Solid Viewport Preview and will not appear in still image or animation renders.

For more details on this feature, see the Viewport & Overlays page

docs.title: EEVEE Render Engine Tips
docs.text: To allow the Segment Display emission to interact with the scene in EEVEE — similar to the Cycles engine — enable the Raytracing option in Properties > Render Properties.

docs.title: "VFont -> Node" Warnings
docs.text:
When using the Segment Display add-on, you may occasionally see the following messages in the Blender System Console:

Failed to add relation "VFont -> Node"
Could not find op_from: ComponentKey(VFBfont Regular, GENERIC_DATABLOCK)

These are technical warnings from Blender's Dependency Graph (Depsgraph). They occur when Blender attempts to rebuild the internal connection map between objects and fonts while a script or asset is being reloaded. Because the add-on uses complex, nested Geometry Node groups to generate dynamic text, Blender sometimes tries to link the Font datablock to the node tree before the font has been fully registered.

This is most common when:

  • Reloading scripts using F8 or the "Reload Scripts" operator while the add-on is active.
  • Reverting or restarting the current Blender project file. Linking or re-importing the display asset from a library.

Should you be worried? No. These messages are non-fatal, purely cosmetic, and do not affect your final output. The fonts referenced in these warnings are only used during the development stage for math, time, and numbering debug purposes. The Segment Display add-on is built entirely using custom meshes and curves, not fonts; it does not rely on these system fonts for the final generated geometry or rendering. Blender's dependency graph recovers automatically once the reload is complete.

To resolve: Simply save and restart Blender, or open a fresh file. Since the add-on's functionality is not affected, you can safely ignore these messages during your workflow.

See the current issue on Blender Developer

docs.title: Viewport & Overlays
docs.text: In complex 3D scenes, constantly switching between viewport shading modes to check your segment display can slow you down. Real LED panels are visible from across a room, but in Blender's Solid viewport mode, material-based effects like emission aren't rendered. SegDisp Pro includes viewport utilities that let you preview your display without leaving Solid mode, so you don't have to switch to Material or Rendered view just to see your results, keeping performance smooth even in busy scenes. Additional overlays let you visualize inactive segments for easier layout and snap-align your display to other objects. This section covers all viewport and overlay inputs across two groups: Solid Viewport Preview and Overlay helpers.

docs.title: Viewport | Solid Preview
docs.text:
[1] Solid Viewport Preview: Allows the display results to be shown in Blender's "Solid" viewport shading mode by switching the Object Color Type to Attribute/Vertex. Useful when working in busy scenes where switching to Material or Rendered view would impact performance.

[2] Led Color / Base Color: Sets the temporary vertex colors used for LED (active) segments and the Display Base, respectively, in Solid viewport mode.

Solid Viewport Preview operates at the Blender level, outside the add-on itself.

Enabling it switches the Object Color Type to Attribute/Vertex across the entire scene — not just for the segment display object. As a result, all other objects in your scene will also adopt this color method, which may alter their appearance in Solid viewport mode. Use this option as a temporary result checker.

Info

If you switch the Object Color Type to Attribute manually from the Blender > Viewport Shading panel, the vertex color on the segment display object may not appear. This is because the Solid Viewport Preview button has not been toggled.

See the Troubleshooting page for the Solid Viewport Preview

docs.title: Ghost Segments
docs.text:
[3] Toggles the visibility of inactive segments to help determine digit boundaries when "Display Base" is not enabled.

Ghost segments are not visible in final renders.

docs.title: Snap Guides
docs.text:
[4] Displays alignment guidelines when 3D viewport Snap is enabled, helping you align the segment display object with other scene items.

Snap Guides

Snap Guides are optimized for use with the Highlighted Snap Target set to Vertex and Edge. Additionally, the Highlighted Snap Base must be set to Center, Median, or Active from the Blender Snap menu.

Blender Limitation

Snap Guides use wireframe geometry, which Blender does not display when the viewport Object Color Type is set to Attribute/Vertex. Because Solid Viewport Preview requires this mode, both features cannot be active at the same time.
